plain: A researcher named Clas Svahn tells how, after the death of an American writer named William Corliss, he got hold of Corliss's papers and brought them from the United States to Sweden. Corliss, Svahn says, wrote a series of books called the Sourcebook Project, which gathered strange and unexplained reports, so his files would matter to anyone hunting for old evidence of unexplained things.
